references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the cities of refuge that were to be given to the Levites are mentioned, where a manslayer could seek protection.
Describes how the congregation was to judge between the manslayer and the avenger of blood, and how the manslayer was to be brought back to the city of refuge.
Moses appointed three cities of refuge east of the Jordan where a manslayer could flee and remain alive.
Detailed instructions about the cities of refuge and their function in protecting someone who killed another unintentionally from the avenger of blood.
Joshua appoints the cities of refuge that the Lord had commanded through Moses, where the manslayer could stand before the congregation for judgment.
The basic law concerning refuge for one who kills without intent, as opposed to one who kills with premeditation.
The book of Hebrews uses the image of fleeing to a city of refuge as a picture of the salvation we have in Christ, our hope.
